judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration clause plus a precedence rule ('this Agreement shall govern'); the internal cross-reference to 'Article 11' for the enumeration of Contract Documents is wrong, since the enumeration sits in Article 15. That misdirection plus the undefined reach of 'other Contract Documents' gives a modest textual foothold.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1, which resolves inconsistencies by requiring the better quality/greater quantity per the Architect's interpretation, and against A201 1.2.1 treating the documents as complementary; those rules point in a different direction from a flat 'Agreement governs' hierarchy. That is a real, though modest, tension across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short obligation to execute the Work with a carve-out for what is 'specifically indicated in the Contract Documents to be the responsibility of others'; the carve-out is bounded by a specificity requirement. Little to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum expressly replaces Article 2 (c099) with a longer version adding staffing and supervision duties, so the original text is superseded rather than contradicted. Low residual risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fill-in reads 'Approximately the Fifteenth of July' — 'approximately' leaves the commencement date indeterminate, and the Owner's mortgage/lien time requirement is left blank. Naming 'approximately' as the vague term is straightforward.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 4.1 (c100) revises this to 'July 15, 2002, pending approval of permits', and A201 8.1.2 says the date of commencement 'is the date established in the Agreement'; the two dates and the permit condition do not align cleanly. A genuine but secondary inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line measuring rule tied to the date of commencement; definite and mechanical. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 8.1.1 (Contract Time definition) and Agreement 4.1/4.3; it fits without friction. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The completion deadline is filled in as 'five hundred ___ calendar days', an incomplete number, and the alternative 'or as follows' line is empty. An unfinished duration is precisely the kind of mechanical defect a court must fill.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 4.3 (c101) fixes Substantial Completion at November 30, 2003, which does not match a day-count run from a commencement date that is itself conditional; A201 8.1.1 and 8.2.1 depend on a determinate Contract Time. The overlap of two different completion formulas is a real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contract Sum is the Cost of the Work as defined in Article 7 plus the Contractor's Fee' is a definitional equation, but it leaves the Contract Sum open-ended and depends entirely on Article 7's contested boundaries. The phrase 'in current funds' and the absence of any stated sum invite argument about what the Owner actually promised to pay.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 (c008), where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is filled in as 'N/A', and against A201 9.1.1, which says the Contract Sum 'is stated in the Agreement' — but no sum is stated anywhere. That mismatch, compounded by 8.1.8, 12.1.5 and 12.1.7.1 all keying payment to a GMP that does not exist, is a serious whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Fee is stated as a flat 'Three Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars ($380,000)' with the bracketed instruction to describe the method of adjustment for changes left unanswered. Whether a lump-sum fee is fixed regardless of how far the Work grows is exactly the ambiguity the omission creates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.4 (equitable adjustment where 'no specific provision is made in Paragraph 5.1'), 12.1.7.3 and 13.2.2 (which compute the fee as a ratio of a fixed-sum fee), and First Addendum 8.1.8 (fee covers all overhead); these machinery clauses presuppose an adjustment method this clause omits. A real relational gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The guaranteed maximum is filled in as 'N/A Dollars ($ N/A)', while the same paragraph declares that costs exceeding the Guaranteed Maximum Price 'shall be paid by the Contractor without reimbursement'. A blank-as-'N/A' cap is both a mechanical defect and a lexical puzzle: does it mean no cap, or no guarantee at all?
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.8, 12.1.5, 12.1.6, 12.1.7.1-.2, 13.2, 13.4 and 6.1, every one of which operates by reference to a Guaranteed Maximum Price; with the figure 'N/A' those provisions cannot be applied as written. This is the clearest whole-instrument incoherence in the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blank fill-in for alternates with only the AIA bracketed instruction remaining; there is no operative content to be ambiguous about. Emptiness is a gap rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the GMP it purports to qualify is itself 'N/A'; the accepted-alternates recital therefore has nothing to attach to. Modest relational weakness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unit prices, if any, are as follows:' with nothing following — a pure blank. No term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.3.9 and 7.3.3.2, which both contemplate unit prices 'stated in the Contract Documents'; with none stated those routes are simply unavailable. Low but not zero.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Allowances, if any, are as follows:' left blank; only the drafting instruction survives. Nothing on the face to argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 3.8.1-3.8.3, which require the Contractor to include 'all allowances stated in the Contract Documents' and adjust the Contract Sum when costs differ; the blank leaves that whole apparatus idle. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Assumptions, if any, on which the Guaranteed Maximum Price is based are as follows:' with no assumptions listed. The blank removes the basis on which any price adjustment argument would rest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 (GMP 'N/A') and 5.2.6 (further development of Drawings); with no assumptions recorded and no GMP figure, the fast-track cost-growth disputes contemplated by First Addendum 6.5 have no documentary anchor. A real, if diffuse, gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause turns on 'reasonably inferable therefrom' and excludes 'such things as changes in scope, systems, kinds and quality of materials, finishes or equipment' — an open-ended 'such things as' catch-all against a list, plus the inherently contestable 'further development' boundary. Both the vague standard and the list scope are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 6.5, which sets up a fast-track pricing procedure in which increased costs from development of the Drawings become part of the Cost of the Work, and against 5.2.1 (GMP 'N/A'); the two treat design development in opposite ways. Genuine relational tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive routing clause ('may be determined by any of the methods listed in Subparagraph 7.3.3 of A201'). The permissive 'may' with several methods is mildly open but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the GMP being adjusted is 'N/A', and against Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1, which makes Change Orders the exclusive route; the adjustment mechanism has no baseline to adjust. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional mapping of 'cost' and 'fee' between this Agreement and A201, with an exception for cost-plus subcontracts. Dense but internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.3 and A201 7.3.3/7.3.6; the mapping is expressly reconciled and says it 'shall not be modified by Articles 5, 7 and 8'. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says 'fee' and 'a reasonable allowance for overhead and profit' shall mean 'the Contractor's Fee as defined in Subparagraph 5.1.1' — but the Fee is defined in 5.1.2, not 5.1.1. That is a plain mechanical mis-cross-reference that changes what the sentence points to.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.1.1 (Contract Sum) and 5.1.2 (Contractor's Fee): the referenced subparagraph defines a different thing entirely, and 13.4 refers correctly to 'Subparagraphs 5.1.2 and Paragraph 6.4'. The inconsistent internal citation is a genuine relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Triggered where 'no specific provision is made in Paragraph 5.1' or where changes cause 'substantial inequity', with the Fee then 'equitably adjusted'; 'substantial inequity' and 'equitably adjusted' are open standards a court must fill. The trigger itself is contestable because 5.1.2 states a bare lump sum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.1.2 (flat $380,000 with no adjustment method stated) and 12.1.7.3/13.2.2 (ratio computation for a fixed-sum fee); whether 5.1 does or does not 'make specific provision' is exactly what the other clauses leave unclear. A real interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Costs necessarily incurred by the Contractor in the proper performance of the Work' at rates 'not higher than the standard paid at the place of the Project' — 'necessarily', 'proper' and 'standard paid at the place of the Project' are each contestable benchmarks. The closing 'shall include only the items set forth in this Article 7' also sets up an expressio unius fight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibits A, B and C, which set the Contractor's own equipment and labor rates and say they 'are based upon standard rates paid at the place of the Project'; whether a self-published rate sheet satisfies the standard is left open. Also checked 8.1.7's catch-all exclusion. Genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Wages of workers 'directly employed' at the site or, with approval, at off-site workshops; the boundaries are drawn by approval requirements. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.1 (salaries of personnel at the principal office excluded) and Exhibit B labor rate sheet; the two fit. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimburses supervisory/administrative wages 'when stationed at the site with the Owner's approval'; the accompanying instruction to identify principal-office personnel 'in Article 14' was never completed. The unfilled option leaves a gap rather than a competing meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.1, which excludes principal-office personnel 'except as specifically provided in Subparagraphs 7.2.2 and 7.2.3 or as may be provided in Article 14' — Article 14 contains no such provision, and First Addendum 8.1.8 puts senior management and administrative support inside the Fee. A real cross-reference failure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Wages of personnel expediting production 'but only for that portion of their time required for the Work' — a proportionality limit that is measurable if disputed. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.1 and First Addendum 8.1.8; the express carve-out in 8.1.1 preserves this item, so it harmonises. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimburses taxes, insurance and benefits required by law, plus 'customary benefits such as sick leave, medical and health benefits, holidays, vacations and pensions' — a 'such as' list that invites ejusdem generis argument about what else is 'customary'. Modest but nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.2.1-7.2.3 (the wage base it cross-references) and First Addendum 8.1.8; the cross-reference works. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Costs of materials 'incorporated or to be incorporated' in the completed construction, including transportation and storage. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.5.6 (off-site storage) and 12.1.7.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable waste and spoilage' is an open standard, and the disposition of unused excess materials ('shall become the Owner's property ... or, at the Owner's option, shall be sold') creates two alternatives without a mechanism for electing. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.1/9.2, which credit amounts realized from sales of surplus materials to the Owner as a deduction from the Cost of the Work; the two overlap but reconcile. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on 'hand tools not customarily owned by construction workers' and on whether items are 'fully consumed', with cost for previously used items being 'fair market value'. 'Customarily owned' and 'fully consumed' are genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibit C, which says the cost of all hand tools not customarily owned by construction workers 'shall be borne by the Contractor' while adding a flat 5% to payroll to cover them; that directly cuts against reimbursing such tools as a Cost of the Work here. A real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Rental charges for equipment 'whether rented from the Contractor or others', subject to the Owner's prior approval of rates and quantities. Self-rental at self-set rates is an obvious pressure point but the approval condition contains it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibit A (the Contractor's own equipment rate sheet), Exhibit C (rental rates 'based upon standard rates paid at the place of the Project') and 8.1.5; whether the exhibits constitute the required prior approval is left unresolved. Genuine interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Costs of removal of debris from the site' — a single, concrete item. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibit D, which treats rubbish hauling and tipping fees as 'Subcontract' costs for excise-tax purposes; a classification overlap only. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of communication and reproduction costs plus 'reasonable petty cash expenses of the site office'; 'reasonable' is soft but the enumeration is concrete. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 8.1.8, which puts 'all main office expenses including telephone, postage, supplies, facsimiles, stationery' inside the Contractor's Fee and bars direct reimbursement under Article 7; the site-office/main-office line is exactly where these two collide. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of the reasonable expenses ... incurred while traveling in discharge of duties connected with the Work' — 'reasonable' and 'connected with' are soft, but the item is narrow. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.6.9 (relocation and temporary living allowances, requiring Owner approval) and 8.1.2; the absence of an approval requirement here, where the neighbouring clause has one, is a mild inconsistency. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Off-site storage at 'a mutually acceptable location, if approved in advance by the Owner' — the approval condition makes it self-policing. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.7.2 and A201 9.3.2, both of which condition payment for off-site storage on written agreement and insurance; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of insurance and bond premiums that can be directly attributed to this Contract' — 'directly attributed' is a genuine allocation standard that two parties could apply very differently. Nameable but narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibit D, which fixes the general liability premium at a flat '1% of the total labor and subcontractors' costs' regardless of what is actually attributable; a flat formula and an attribution test are not the same rule. Real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sales, use or similar taxes imposed by a governmental authority that are related to the Work' — 'similar' and 'related to' are open, though the item is conventional. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibit D, which fixes how the Hawaii General Excise Tax is computed and which costs are exempt, and against A201 3.6.1 (Contractor 'shall pay' such taxes); the allocation of the same tax appears in three places. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permit and inspection fees 'for which the Contractor is required by the Contract Documents to pay' — the qualifier ties it to an identifiable obligation. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 3.7.1 (Contractor secures and pays for the building permit) and A201 2.2.2 (Owner pays for easements and assessments); the division is expressly drawn. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Laboratory fees except those related to defective Work under A201 13.5.3 'or other provisions of the Contract Documents' and not within 7.7.1 — the open-ended 'or other provisions' broadens the exception indefinitely. A modest general-versus-specific point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 13.5.3 and 7.7.1/8.1.6; the exclusions interlock, though the unnamed 'other provisions' leaves the boundary soft. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long clause with an internal carve-out: legal defence costs, judgments and settlements 'shall not be included in the calculation of the Contractor's Fee or subject to the Guaranteed Maximum Price', then a conditional exclusion keyed to the last sentence of A201 3.17.1. The layered exceptions are hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the GMP is 'N/A' (so a carve-out from the GMP has no referent), and against A201 3.17.1, which allocates royalty and infringement risk differently. Real relational weakness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Data processing costs related to the Work' — brief and open at the edges but unremarkable. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 8.1.8, which places 'all accounting services' inside the Fee and bars direct reimbursement; data processing sits close to that line. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lost deposits 'for causes other than the Contractor's negligence or failure to fulfill a specific responsibility' — a fault-based carve-out that mirrors 8.1.6. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.6, which excludes costs due to the Contractor's negligence or failure to fulfil a specific responsibility; the two are consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimburses legal, mediation and arbitration costs 'other than those arising from disputes between the Owner and Contractor', with Owner approval 'not to be unreasonably withheld'. The Owner/Contractor carve-out is clear but 'arising from' can be stretched.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.5/4.6 (mediation and arbitration between Owner and Contractor) and 8.1.6; the carve-out lines up with those. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Relocation and temporary living allowances 'in accordance with the Contractor's standard personnel policy ... if approved by the Owner' — the incorporated policy is an external, unproduced document. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.1 and First Addendum 8.1.8; the Owner-approval condition keeps it inside the reimbursement scheme. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A residual category — 'other costs incurred in the performance of the Work if and to the extent approved in advance in writing by the Owner'. As a catch-all sitting after a long enumerated list it is the classic general-versus-specific spot, though the written-approval condition narrows it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.7 ('any cost not specifically and expressly described in Article 7' is excluded); a written-approval catch-all and an express-description-only exclusion pull against each other. Genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Emergency costs as provided in A201 10.6, without qualification as to fault. Short and conventional on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 7.7.2 [Revision] (c104), which adds two fault-based limitations that are absent here; both versions sit in the instrument and the Supplementary Conditions preamble preserves unaltered provisions. Real overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Repair costs for damaged or nonconforming Work, provided not caused by 'negligence or failure to fulfill a specific responsibility' and 'only to the extent ... not recoverable ... from insurance, sureties, Subcontractors or suppliers'. The recoverability test is workable but fact-heavy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 7.7.3 [Revision] (c105), which adds a proviso about absence of collectible insurance due to the Contractor's failure to maintain it; the revised and original texts coexist in the document. Real overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory line ('The Cost of the Work shall not include:'). Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.1's closing sentence limiting the Cost of the Work to Article 7 items; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes principal-office salaries 'except as specifically provided in Subparagraphs 7.2.2 and 7.2.3 or as may be provided in Article 14' — the exception invokes a provision that was never completed. That dangling exception is a nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 14 of the Agreement, where 14.6 'Other provisions' is blank and the First Addendum's 14.6 is a set of representations, not a personnel schedule; the exception therefore points nowhere, while First Addendum 8.1.8 puts such personnel inside the Fee. A real cross-reference failure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes 'expenses of the Contractor's principal office and offices other than the site office' — a clean binary line. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.5.4 (site-office telephone, postage and petty cash reimbursed) and First Addendum 8.1.8 (all main office expenses in the Fee); the site/main-office boundary is where these meet. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Overhead and general expenses, except as may be expressly included in Article 7' — 'overhead' and 'general expenses' are undefined, and the exception is only as clear as Article 7. A nameable but ordinary softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 8.1.8, which enumerates what the Fee covers, against Exhibit C's flat 5% hand-tool add-on to payroll, and against 7.5.1/7.5.4; whether the 5% is 'overhead' or an Article 7 item is left open. Genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes rental costs of machinery and equipment 'except as specifically provided in Subparagraph 7.5.2'; a precise carve-out. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.5.2 and Exhibits A and C, which set the Contractor's own rental rates for its own equipment; whether self-rental at published rates falls inside the 7.5.2 exception is not resolved. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes costs due to 'negligence or failure to fulfill a specific responsibility' of the Contractor and its chain, 'except as provided in Subparagraph 7.7.3'. The fault standard is conventional, if fact-bound.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.7.3 and First Addendum 7.7.3 [Revision]; the exception is expressly cross-referenced and coherent, though the Addendum's added proviso complicates it. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any cost not specifically and expressly described in Article 7' is a total residual exclusion sitting against a long enumerated list — an expressio unius provision of exactly the kind courts are asked to construe. 'Specifically and expressly' sets a demanding threshold.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.7.1, which reimburses 'other costs' approved in writing by the Owner; a written approval cannot make a cost 'expressly described in Article 7', so the two rules pull apart. Genuine conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes 'costs, other than costs included in Change Orders approved by the Owner, that would cause the Guaranteed Maximum Price to be exceeded'. On its own it is a clean rule — but it is entirely parasitic on a GMP figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the GMP is 'N/A', and against First Addendum 8.1.8, which replaces subparagraph 8.1.8 with an entirely different provision about the Fee covering overhead; both the referent and the numbering are broken. Serious relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Splits cash discounts between Owner and Contractor on two enumerated conditions, then sweeps 'Trade discounts, rebates, refunds and amounts received from sales of surplus materials and equipment' to the Owner and requires the Contractor to 'make provisions so that they can be secured'. The list is specific but the closing duty to 'make provisions' has no ascertainable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 9.1.1 [New], which forbids the Contractor from obtaining discounts for its own benefit without seven days' notice and an Owner opportunity to fund them, and against 7.4.2 (proceeds of unused excess materials credited to the Owner); the Addendum materially narrows the 'otherwise ... accrue to the Contractor' half of this clause. Real interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Amounts that accrue to the Owner in accordance with Paragraph 9.1 shall be credited to the Owner as a deduction from the Cost of the Work.' A single definite accounting instruction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.1, 7.4.2 and 5.1.1 (Contract Sum is Cost of the Work plus Fee); crediting against the Cost of the Work is consistent throughout. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on what the Contractor 'does not customarily perform with the Contractor's own personnel' and preserves a right not to contract with anyone to whom it has 'reasonable objection' — both are nameable open standards, and 'customarily' governs the whole allocation of self-performed work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 6.5 [New], which prescribes a different procurement route (Preliminary Budget, at least two bids, suppliers 'named by Owner or Architect and reasonably acceptable to Contractor', Change Orders adjusting the Contract Sum) from this clause's 'the Owner shall then determine ... which bids will be accepted'. Two bidding regimes for the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-element test — recommended, qualified, and a conforming bid 'without reservations or exceptions' — followed by a precise difference-based adjustment. Definite as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price this clause adjusts is stated as 'N/A', and against First Addendum 6.5 [New], which routes bid-based adjustments to the Contract Sum instead; the remedy operates on a figure that does not exist. Serious relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States the default one-calendar-month period and then trails off into 'or as follows:' with nothing following, so the alternative invited by the form was never supplied. The default still reads sensibly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.3, whose application and payment days are illegible or unfilled, and 12.1.6 (percentage of completion 'as of the end of the period covered'); the period is the one payment variable that is fixed. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three operative numbers — the day of the month by which the Application must be received, the day of the following month for payment, and the fallback number of days — are all garbled or unreadable here, so the payment timetable cannot be applied from the text. That incompleteness is a mechanical defect that changes what the provision requires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.6.1 (payment 'within the time provided in the Contract Documents') and 14.1.1.3/9.7.1 (stop-work and termination rights keyed to 'the time stated in the Contract Documents'), and First Addendum 12.2.2, which fixes only final payment; several remedies depend on a date this clause fails to fix. Real gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists payrolls, petty cash accounts and receipted invoices and then adds 'any other evidence required by the Owner or Architect' — an unqualified catch-all after enumerated specifics — followed by a three-term arithmetic test whose components must be read carefully.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.4 [New], which adds subcontractor statements and lien waivers 'all in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' but qualifies its residual item with 'reasonably may require'; the two catch-alls carry different standards for the same submission. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the schedule of values to allocate 'the entire Guaranteed Maximum Price' among portions of the Work, with the Fee shown separately, in such form 'as the Architect may require'. Clear as a mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A', and First Addendum 6.5 [New], which substitutes a Preliminary Budget with an Itemized Schedule of Values representing the 'current best estimate of the Contract Sum'; the sum this schedule must allocate does not exist. Serious incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lesser-of test between actual completion and an expense-to-allocated-share ratio, including expense 'for which the Contractor has made or intends to make actual payment'. The arithmetic is stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 ('N/A' Guaranteed Maximum Price) and 12.1.5; limb (2) divides by 'the share of the Guaranteed Maximum Price allocated to that portion of the Work', which cannot be computed on this contract. Real defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in — 'the amount of each progress payment shall be computed' — whose closing 'as follows:' is lost in the marginal text here; it carries no independent obligation. Minor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the six clauses it introduces (12.1.7.1-.6) and 12.1.5; the computation it opens rests on the Guaranteed Maximum Price stated as 'N/A' in 5.2.1. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of the Guaranteed Maximum Price properly allocable to completed Work' — 'properly allocable' is the soft term, but the multiplication it prescribes is otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A', and 12.1.5/12.1.6, which build the same computation on the same missing figure; the first and largest component of every progress payment has no defined base. Serious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds the portion of the Guaranteed Maximum Price allocable to materials stored at the site, or off site 'if approved in advance by the Owner' at 'a location agreed upon in writing'. Conditions are explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.5.6 (off-site storage 'at a mutually acceptable location, if approved in advance by the Owner'), A201 9.3.2 (procedures 'satisfactory to the Owner' to establish title) and 5.2.1's 'N/A' Guaranteed Maximum Price; three formulations of the same off-site storage condition plus a missing base figure. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retainage figure is entered as 'N/A percent (N/A %)', which on its face means no retainage is held on the Fee; entering 'N/A' into a percentage blank leaves it arguable whether the parties meant zero or meant to say nothing at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.7.3 [Revision], which restates the identical clause with 'five percent (5%)' retainage, and against Article 1 of the Agreement, which provides that where another Contract Document is inconsistent with the Agreement 'this Agreement shall govern' — the amendment and the priority clause point opposite ways on the same number. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subtract the aggregate of previous payments made by the Owner.' Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.7.1-.3 and 13.2.3, which use the identical subtraction; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subtracts a shortfall 'indicated by the Contractor' in the 12.1.4 documentation 'or resulting from errors subsequently discovered by the Owner's accountants' — the second limb is open-ended in time and has no verification or dispute mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.4 and First Addendum 12.1.4 [New] (which enlarges the required documentation) and 12.1.9/Article 11 (Owner's accountants acting 'in the sole interest of the Owner'); the deduction depends on documents whose content is set by two different provisions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subtracts amounts for which the Architect 'has withheld or nullified a Certificate for Payment as provided in Paragraph 9.5' of A201. A pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.5.1-9.5.3 and Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1 (Owner concurrence required wherever the Architect acts); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph is numbered '12.1.9' although the following paragraph carries the same number, so the subcontractor retainage rule and the Architect's-reliance rule share an identifier; it also ends in an agreement to agree on a 'mutually acceptable procedure'. Both the misnumbering and the open procedure are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.7.3 ('N/A' retainage on the Fee), First Addendum 12.1.7.3 (5%) and A201 9.6.2 (pay-through 'reflecting percentages actually retained'); the retainage figures across the documents do not line up, and the duplicate numbering makes cross-references to 12.1.9 ambiguous. Real difficulty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully hedged statement that the Architect may rely on the Contractor's information and is not deemed to have audited it, with verification reserved to the Owner's accountants 'acting in the sole interest of the Owner'. Definite, though it shares its paragraph number with the preceding provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.4.2 (the same disclaimers) and Article 11 (accounting records and audit rights); consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Final payment, constituting the entire unpaid balance of the Contract Sum, shall be made ... when:' — a two-condition gateway, definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.2.1 [New], which adds a third condition (a duly published and recorded Notice of Completion), Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 (no final Certificate until all warranties are received and accepted by the Owner), and 5.1.1/5.2.1, where no Contract Sum figure is stated; the conditions are spread across three documents and the 'unpaid balance' has no fixed referent. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires full performance except the correction obligation 'and to satisfy other requirements, if any, which extend beyond final payment' — an unspecified residual category attached to a completion condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 14.6 [New] (warranties that expressly 'survive ... the final completion of the Work') and A201 12.2.2/9.10.4; the surviving requirements exist but are enumerated elsewhere. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A final Certificate for Payment has been issued by the Architect.' A single objective event.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 (the final Certificate 'will not be issued ... until all warranties and guarantees have been received and accepted by the Owner') and 12.2.3; issuance is conditioned elsewhere but not inconsistently. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes final payment at 'no later than 30 days after the issuance of the Architect's final Certificate for Payment, or as follows:' and then leaves the alternative blank, so the form invites a substitute that never appears in this document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.2.2 [Revision], which sets final payment at fifty days after recordation of the Notice of Completion or five business days after a lien-free title endorsement, whichever is earlier, and against Article 1 ('If anything in the other Contract Documents is inconsistent with this Agreement, this Agreement shall govern'); two irreconcilable final-payment deadlines with a priority clause favouring the older one. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sequenced 30-day/seven-day review procedure ending with an express statement that its time periods 'supersede those stated in Subparagraph 9.4.1' of A201. Definite and self-aware.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.4.1 (which it expressly displaces), 12.2.1/First Addendum 12.2.1 [New], Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 and First Addendum 12.2.2 [Revision]; the final-payment gateway is described in four documents with different triggers and clocks. Real interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Gives a 30-day window to demand arbitration and then, in the same sentence, describes it as 'this 10-day period', so the forfeiture deadline is stated twice with two different numbers; a mismatch of that kind in a provision that makes an amount 'binding on the Contractor' is exactly the sort of mechanical error that changes meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.5/4.6 (mediation as a condition precedent to arbitration and the demand-timing rules) and 12.2.3; this clause lets the Contractor go straight to arbitration 'without a further decision of the Architect', which cuts across the A201 claims machinery. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimburses post-final-payment correction costs 'but not in excess of the Guaranteed Maximum Price' and requires savings to be recalculated 'as provided in Paragraph 5.2', a cross-reference that is garbled here. Both the cap and the reference are doubtful on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A' and the savings-participation insert was left blank, and against A201 12.2.2/12.2.5; the clause conditions payment on a cap and a savings arrangement that this contract never created. Serious relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Caps convenience-termination payment at the for-cause amount 'except that the Contractor's Fee shall be calculated as if the Work had been fully completed by the Contractor, including a reasonable estimate of the Cost of the Work for Work not actually completed'. The 'reasonable estimate' standard is open and assigned to nobody, and the interaction of a cap with that exception is not obvious from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 14.4.3, which entitles the Contractor on convenience termination to payment for Work executed, termination costs and 'reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed', and against A201 4.3.10, whose consequential damages waiver applies 'without limitation, to all consequential damages due to either party's termination in accordance with Article 14'. Three provisions give three different measures of the same payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A double cap on for-cause termination payment — it 'shall not cause the Guaranteed Maximum Price to be exceeded, nor shall it exceed an amount calculated as follows'. The structure is clear; the difficulty is that the first limb rests on a figure that was never supplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is filled in as 'N/A', and against A201 14.2.4, which measures the same payment against 'the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum' and requires the Architect to certify it; the first cap has no referent and the two computations differ. Real defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Take the Cost of the Work incurred by the Contractor to the date of termination' — one arithmetic step resting on a term defined in Article 7. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 7's definition of the Cost of the Work and Article 8's exclusions; consistent, and the exclusions bound the figure. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Computes the Fee 'at the rate stated in Subparagraph 5.1.2 or, if the Contractor's Fee is stated as a fixed sum ... an amount that bears the same ratio to that fixed-sum Fee as the Cost of the Work at the time of termination bears to a reasonable estimate of the probable Cost of the Work upon its completion'. The estimate is undefined, unassigned and outcome-determinative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.1.2, where the Fee is a flat $380,000 with no rate stated, so only the second limb can ever operate, and against 12.1.7.3, which uses the same untethered 'reasonable estimate' for progress payments. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subtract the aggregate of previous payments made by the Owner.' Definite and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.7.4, which prescribes the identical subtraction in the progress-payment computation; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fair compensation, either by purchase or rental at the election of the Owner' for equipment the Owner elects to retain — an open valuation standard with no mechanism for fixing the amount or resolving disagreement. Nameable, though conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.2.1 (which this clause expressly excepts), Exhibit A's equipment rate sheet (which supplies rental rates that may or may not be the 'fair' measure) and A201 5.4.1/14.2.2.2 on assignment of subcontracts; the assignment machinery aligns but the valuation route does not. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: On suspension the Guaranteed Maximum Price and Contract Time 'shall be increased as provided in Subparagraph 14.3.2 of AIA Document A201-1997 except that the term "profit" shall be understood to mean the Contractor's Fee as described in Subparagraphs 5.1.2 and Paragraph 6.4'. The redefinition is explicit and the cross-references are correct.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 ('N/A' Guaranteed Maximum Price) and 5.1.2 (a flat lump-sum Fee with no adjustment method); an instruction to increase a maximum price that does not exist, using a 'profit' that is a fixed sum, cannot be applied as written. Real defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reading rule: a reference to A201 or another Contract Document 'refers to that provision as amended or supplemented by other provisions of the Contract Documents'. Broad but purposive and clear in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Supplementary Conditions preamble ('the unaltered provision of the General Conditions shall remain in effect') and Article 1's precedence rule; three reading rules coexist and this one tends to defeat Article 1's 'this Agreement shall govern' where a supplement amends an A201 reference. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest runs 'at the rate stated below, or in the absence thereof, at the legal rate prevailing from time to time at the place where the Project is located', and the rate line is blank or unreadable. The fallback rescues the clause, but the unfilled blank is a nameable mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.7.1, which adds interest 'as provided for in the Contract Documents' to shutdown, delay and start-up costs, and against 12.1.3/12.2.2, whose payment dates are themselves incomplete; the rate has a fallback but the date from which interest runs does not. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens' and 'Mary Williamson' as the Owner's representative without saying whether they act jointly or severally, or whose act binds the Owner. A plural designation with no allocation of authority is a genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 14.3 [Revised] ('Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson') and Supplementary Conditions 2.1.1.1, which states the authorized representative 'is Mary Williamson' but then allows action by 'Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson'; three provisions in three documents identify the representative differently. Real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Contractor's representative is given as 'John F. Maurer, EME, succeeded by Keith H. Willis, Senior Project Manager' — a designation with a built-in but undated succession, so who held the role at any given moment is not fixed by the text. Modest but nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.5, which forbids changing a representative without ten days' written notice to the other party; a succession written into the Agreement sits awkwardly with that requirement, and First Addendum Article 2 [Revised] separately requires a designated supervisory employee. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Neither the Owner's nor the Contractor's representative shall be changed without ten days' written notice to the other party.' Symmetrical, short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.3/14.4, First Addendum 14.3 [Revised] and Supplementary Conditions 2.1.1.1, each of which names a different set of Owner actors; whether those later designations are 'changes' triggering this notice requirement is left unanswered. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other provisions:' followed by nothing at all — a heading with no operative content, so there is no term capable of bearing two meanings. The defect, if any, is emptiness rather than ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.1, which excludes principal-office personnel costs 'except as specifically provided in Subparagraphs 7.2.2 and 7.2.3 or as may be provided in Article 14' — an exception now pointing at an empty paragraph — and against First Addendum 14.6 [New], which uses the same number for representations and warranties. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory enumeration line excluding Modifications issued after execution. Plain and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 1 and A201 1.1.1, which excludes documents not 'specifically enumerated in the Agreement'; consistent in form, although the sub-paragraphs it introduces are largely blank or 'TBD'. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the Agreement as this executed 1997 edition of AIA Document A111. A simple identification with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 15.1.1 [Revision], which restates it 'as modified by the First Addendum hereto'; the unrevised text omits the Addendum from the description of the Agreement, which matters under Article 1's precedence rule. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause identifies the General Conditions as 'the 1991 edition of the General Conditions of the Contract for Construction AIA Document A201-1997' — the edition year and the document number in the same sentence contradict each other. That is a mechanical error going directly to which document is incorporated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 15.1.2 [Revision] and the Supplementary Conditions preamble, both of which identify A201, 1997 Edition, and against Articles 6, 7, 12 and 13 of the Agreement, which cite A201-1997 throughout. Real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Points to Specifications 'contained in the Project Manual dated as in Subparagraph 15.1.3' with the section/title/page table left entirely empty. The incorporation is by reference to a volume that the document never describes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 15.1.3, whose Project Manual date is blank and whose document list reads 'TBD', and against A201 1.1.6/1.1.7 (definitions of the Specifications and the Project Manual); the incorporation chain terminates in nothing. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Drawings are as follows, and are dated ___ unless a different date is shown below', with the number/title/date table left blank or 'TBD'. An unlisted, undated set of Drawings is a real gap in identifying the Work the Contractor promised to perform.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 1.1.5 and 1.1.1 (documents must be 'specifically enumerated in the Agreement'), and against First Addendum 6.5 [New] and Supplementary Conditions 3.10.5, which contemplate drawings arriving in later design phases; enumeration and fast-track development do not fit together. Genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists the First Addendum and the Supplementary Conditions as 'Addenda', then excludes portions of Addenda 'relating to bidding requirements' unless separately enumerated. Calling negotiated amendments 'Addenda' is loose, but the exclusion is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 15.1.2 and the Supplementary Conditions preamble, which treat those documents as modifications of the General Conditions rather than bidding addenda, and against Article 1's precedence rule; how they are classified affects whether the Agreement or the amendments govern. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerates Exhibits A through E as Contract Documents, one of which (Exhibit E) is a certificate of liability insurance rather than a contractual term. Listing an evidentiary certificate as an operative document is odd but not ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibit C (hand tools 'borne by the Contractor' yet a 5% payroll add-on), Exhibit D (1% insurance rate and General Excise Tax treatment) and Articles 7 and 8, which allocate the same costs differently, and against Article 1's rule that the Agreement governs over inconsistent documents; this enumeration is what gives the exhibits force and puts them into conflict. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'ARTICLE 16 INSURANCE AND BONDS' followed only by the AIA bracketed instruction — no limits of liability, no bond requirements, nothing completed. A wholly empty article on a subject the form directs the parties to fill in is a nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 11.1.2 (insurance 'for not less than limits of liability specified in the Contract Documents or required by law, whichever coverage is greater'), A201 11.3.1 (minimum limits keyed to Clauses 11.1.1.2 through 11.1.1.5), A201 11.4.2 (boiler insurance 'required in the Contract Documents') and Supplementary Conditions 11.6; the limits all of those provisions assume exist nowhere in the instrument. Real incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard execution recital as to the number of original copies and their delivery to Contractor, Architect and Owner. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 1.5.1, which requires the Contract Documents to be signed by Owner and Contractor and provides for identification of unsigned documents; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital that the Addendum is 'attached to and incorporated by reference in' the Agreement 'dated February 1, 2002', for the purpose of 'modifying, supplementing, and amending certain terms and conditions'. It fixes a date with a precision the Agreement's own date line lacks, and 'certain terms and conditions' identifies nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Agreement's opening date line, which is incomplete in this instrument, and against the Addendum's own execution block ('Executed at ___ this __ day of ___, 2002'); a recital fixing a date that the operative execution block leaves blank is a recital-versus-operative mismatch, and Article 1's precedence rule then has to be applied to an instrument of uncertain date. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds duties to furnish 'only skilled and properly trained staff' and to designate one supervisory employee who 'personally shall supervise and attend to the Work', who may take other work 'only to the extent it does not impair his or her ability to perform this Work, including without limitation, assuring the quality of the Work and maintaining the construction schedule'. 'Properly trained', 'personally' and 'impair' are each soft standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 3.9.1 (a competent superintendent 'in attendance at the Project site during performance of the Work') and A201 10.2.6 (a designated safety member presumed to be the superintendent), and against Agreement 14.4, which names two different Contractor representatives; the staffing designations overlap without being reconciled. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The date of commencement of the work shall be July 15, 2002, pending approval of permits' — 'pending approval of permits' is genuinely ambiguous as to whether the date is fixed or conditional, whose permits are meant, and what follows if approval is late. That phrase is the nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 8.1.2 ('the date of commencement of the Work is the date established in the Agreement'), A201 8.2.2, Agreement 4.2 (Contract Time measured from commencement) and First Addendum 4.3 [Revised] (a fixed November 30, 2003 completion date); a floating start against a fixed finish destabilises the whole time scheme, including the bonus in First Addendum 4.4. Real relational problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed calendar deadline of November 30, 2003, 'subject to adjustments of this Contract Time as provided in the Contract Documents'. Definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the base Agreement 4.3, which measures completion as a (garbled) number of calendar days from commencement, and against 4.1 [Revised], whose commencement is 'pending approval of permits'; a fixed end date and a floating start are not easily reconciled. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner shall pay as a bonus to the Contractor a sum to be determined' — the amount, the determinant and the standard are all missing, and the sum is then 'divided between the key management staff, as determined by the Owner'. A promise to pay an undetermined sum is the paradigm of an unenforceably vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3 [Revised] (the 'established date of Substantial Completion' it references) and A201 9.8.4 (Architect certifies the date); the trigger is identifiable even though the amount is not, and no other clause supplies the figure. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This fast-track clause turns on soft terms throughout — 'Contractor's current best estimate of the Contract Sum', 'industry-standard figures', pricing 'as agreed with Owner', an Owner termination right in 'Owner's sole and absolute discretion' if the Preliminary Budget 'is not acceptable', and Change Orders issued 'as the price for each item ... is refined'. Whether the Preliminary Budget caps anything, and what happens if the parties never refine an item, are live questions on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 (GMP 'N/A'), 5.2.6 (further development already priced into the GMP), 12.1.5 (schedule of values allocating 'the entire Guaranteed Maximum Price') and Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1 (changes only by Change Order, no unjust enrichment); this clause makes design-development cost growth automatically part of the Cost of the Work while those provisions channel and cap it. That is a genuine whole-instrument inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Emergency costs are reimbursable 'only to the extent not ... capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition to Owner or Architect' — a counterfactual preventability test with no benchmark. 'Timely' and 'capable of being prevented' are both nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the unrevised 7.7.2 (c041), which contains no such limits, and against A201 10.6.1, which lets the Contractor act 'at the Contractor's discretion' in an emergency and claim compensation under 4.3 and Article 7; the revision narrows what A201 preserves. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds a proviso that absence of collectible insurance must not be 'due to Contractor's failure to maintain required insurance, or breach of a contract for insurance'. 'Required insurance' is the soft element, given that no limits were ever specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 16 of the Agreement, which is blank as to required insurance limits, and against the unrevised 7.7.3 (c042) and A201 11.1; the proviso depends on a specification the Contract Documents never made. Real gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of what the Fee 'shall cover', closing with 'and none of these items shall be subject to direct reimbursement under Article 7'; the list ends with 'estimating/project purchasing costs and expenses', leaving the outer boundary of 'main office overhead' contestable. The enumeration-versus-general tension is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the base Agreement 8.1.8 (c050), which this revision replaces with an entirely different subject — the GMP-exceeding exclusion simply vanishes — and against 7.5.4, 7.6.1 and 7.6.6, which reimburse telephone, postage, insurance and data processing. Two provisions bearing the same number and saying different things is a real defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A notice-and-opportunity mechanic before the Contractor may take a discount 'for its own benefit'; the seven-day period and the required notice are concrete. Modest softness in 'potential' discount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.1, which already allocates cash discounts by reference to whether the Owner funded the payment; the new clause layers a procedural condition on the same subject without amending 9.1's allocation. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires accompanying items 'all in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' — a pure satisfaction standard with no reasonableness qualifier, in contrast to sub-paragraph (c) below it. That inconsistency in standards within a single clause is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the base Agreement 12.1.4 (c057), which bears the same number and imposes its own substantiation requirements; two provisions numbered 12.1.4 coexist. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed schedule requirement listing exactly what the statement must show, including similar statements from lower-tier suppliers 'when appropriate'. 'When appropriate' is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.3.1 (data substantiating the Contractor's right to payment) and 9.6.2; consistent and cumulative. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete $2,500 threshold for lien waivers 'establishing payment or satisfaction of the payment requested'. The waiver-before-payment sequencing is awkward but the terms are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.10.2 (waivers at final payment) and First Addendum 12.2.2 (lien-free endorsement); the requirements stack coherently. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such other information, documentation, and material as Owner or the Architect reasonably may require' is a residual catch-all following two specific enumerated items — the classic ejusdem generis / expressio unius setting. The reasonableness qualifier limits it but does not fix its reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the base 12.1.4, which similarly allows 'any other evidence required by the Owner or Architect', and A201 9.3.1; the overlap is cumulative. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sets retainage at 'five percent (5%)' and otherwise repeats the fixed-sum-fee ratio using 'a reasonable estimate of the probable Cost of the Work upon its completion'. The estimate standard is soft; the percentage is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the base 12.1.7.3 (c063), which states retainage as 'N/A percent'; the two versions of the same subparagraph give different answers and both sit in the instrument. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds as a condition that 'a Notice of Completion of the Work has been duly published and recorded' — a concrete statutory event. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.2.1's two existing conditions and A201 9.10.1-9.10.2; the addition is cumulative, though it makes final payment turn on a recording the Owner controls. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Final payment is due 'within fifty (50) days after recordation of the Notice of Completion or within five (5) business days after Contractor obtains and presents ... a lien-free endorsement, whichever is earlier'. Both triggers depend on events that may never occur, and 'whichever is earlier' between two contingent events is genuinely ambiguous in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against base 12.2.2 (30 days after the final Certificate for Payment) and 12.2.3; the Agreement and the Addendum give incompatible payment deadlines keyed to different events. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner's representative is Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson' — three alternatives joined by 'or' with no allocation of authority between them. The disjunctive designation is a nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against base 14.3 and Supplementary Conditions 2.1.1.1, which says the authorized representative 'is Mary Williamson' but that actions may be taken by 'Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson'; the three provisions do not match, and 'Mrs. Paul Stephens' and 'Elle M. Stephens' are described inconsistently. Real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A chapeau stating that the following representations are given 'as a material inducement' and 'shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement, any termination ... and the final completion of the Work'. Broad survival language, but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 1's integration clause and A201 1.1.2; the survival language sits comfortably with both. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A solvency and working-capital representation extended to 'the Subcontractors' — a representation about third parties the Contractor may not control or have selected yet. That extension is the only soft point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.1/A201 5.2.1, where subcontractors are selected after execution with Owner input; representing as of signing about the solvency of not-yet-chosen subcontractors is awkward. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capability representation ('has sufficient experience and competence to do so'); an evaluative but conventional warranty. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 3 (relationship of trust and confidence) and A201 3.4; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A licensing representation covering 'all necessary governmental and public and quasi-public authorities having jurisdiction'. The catch-all 'quasi-public' is loose but the substance is verifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 3.7.1 (permits and licenses) and 3.7.2; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A site-visit representation with 'correlated observations with the requirements of the Contract Documents'. Standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 1.5.2 and 3.2.1, which contain materially the same representation; duplication rather than conflict, although A201 3.2.1 says the review is 'not for the purpose of discovering errors'. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Restates the Agreement as A111 1997 'as modified by the First Addendum hereto'. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against base 15.1.1 and Article 1's precedence rule; the revision brings the enumeration up to date. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the General Conditions as A201, 1997 Edition, 'as modified by the Supplementary Conditions thereto'. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against base 15.1.2 (c091), which says '1991 edition'; the two enumerations of the same document disagree on the edition. Real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Incorporates A201 'Articles 1 through 14 inclusive' as fully as if set forth — a bounded incorporation, though A201-1997 in fact runs to Article 14, so the bound is complete. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 1 of the Agreement ('this Agreement shall govern' over inconsistent documents) and Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1; a wholesale incorporation plus a precedence rule plus a better-quality rule is a three-way arrangement. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The following supplements modify, change, delete from, and add to the General Conditions. When any portion ... is modified or ... deleted by these Supplementary Conditions, the unaltered provision of the General Conditions shall remain in effect.' Saying a deleted provision's 'unaltered' part remains in effect is genuinely hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 2.4.1, which restates A201 2.4.1 while dropping its second-notice requirement, and against Article 1's precedence rule; whether the dropped requirement was 'deleted' or remains as an 'unaltered provision' is exactly the question this clause leaves open. Real incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Owner's express written consent wherever the Architect's is required, then disclaims Owner responsibility for means and methods 'notwithstanding any of the rights and authority granted the Owner in the Contract Documents'. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.2.1-4.2.2 (Architect's authority not to be modified without written consent of all three), 3.3.1 and 4.2.3; inserting the Owner into every Architect approval sits awkwardly with A201's allocation. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: On inconsistency the Contractor must 'provide the better quality or greater quantity of Work or comply with the more stringent requirement; either or both in accordance with the Architect's interpretation as approved by the Owner'. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 1 ('if anything in the other Contract Documents is inconsistent with this Agreement, this Agreement shall govern') and A201 1.2.1 (documents are complementary); this clause supplies a third, different rule for the same problem. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional precedence rule for dimensions and drawing scales. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 1.2.1.1's chapeau and A201 1.2.1; consistent as a specific application. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.3.4 (concealed or unknown conditions giving rise to equitable adjustment) and A201 3.2.3/4.3.6 (claims arising from clarifications); a flat no-compensation rule cuts across those claim routes. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires drawings of any 'minor change ... found necessary due to actual field conditions' to be approved before making the change; 'minor' is undefined here. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 7.4.1, which gives the Architect authority to order minor changes not involving adjustment of the Contract Sum or Time; that clause treats minor changes as Architect-initiated, this one as Contractor-initiated. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner's authorized representative is Mary Williamson' followed immediately by a sentence permitting any action to be taken by 'Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 14.3 ('Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens' and 'Mary Williamson') and First Addendum 14.3 [Revised]; three provisions in three documents identify the Owner's representative differently, and 14.5 requires ten days' notice for any change. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single seven-day cure period before the Owner may correct deficiencies and charge the Contractor, subject to prior approval of the Architect. Internally clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Construction Schedule 'as it is developed, shall be deemed attached to Document A111 as a part of the Contract Documents' — a document that becomes contractually binding as it evolves, with no version control. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 15 (enumeration of Contract Documents) and A201 1.1.1 (documents not 'specifically enumerated in the Agreement' are excluded) and A201 1.1.2 (the Contract may be amended 'only by Modification'); a self-attaching document cuts against both. judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires phased cost estimates and revised schedules, each of which 'as they are developed, shall become part of the Contract Documents'. The same self-incorporation problem, plus 'detailed cost estimate' and 'line item budget' left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 6.5 (Preliminary Budget and Itemized Schedule of Values, also to become an exhibit), Agreement Article 15 and A201 1.1.1/1.1.2; three separate self-incorporating budget documents with no precedence rule among them. Real incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires Architect approval of shop drawings and warrants they will be prepared by persons 'possessing expertise and experience in the trade'. Evaluative but ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 3.12.4-3.12.10 and Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1 (Owner's concurrence also required); cumulative rather than contradictory. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed content requirement for time claims plus 'such supporting documentation as the Owner may require'. The open documentation requirement is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.3.7.1 and 4.3.2 (21-day notice); the requirements stack. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As written the clause is close to unreadable — 'shall not be entitled to a separate increase in the Contract Time for each ... of the number of causes of delay which may have concurrent or interrelated effects' — and 'concurrent or interrelated' is undefined. judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause bars any increase based on 'course of conduct or dealings', 'express or implied acceptance of alterations or additions', and 'no claim that the Owner has been unjustly enriched ... whether or not there is, in fact, any unjust enrichment' — an unusual attempt to contract out of a restitutionary claim, opening with the carve-out 'Except as permitted in Paragraph 7.3 and Paragraph 9.7.1'. judgments.reasoning_cat1: Makes a Change Order 'a final settlement of all matters relating to the change ... including, but not limited to, all direct and indirect costs' and all adjustments to the Contract Sum, Fee and Schedule. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 7.3.8 (interim determinations subject to later claim), A201 4.3.6 and Supplementary Conditions 7.1.3.1; a per-change final settlement rule sits awkwardly with A201's provisional pricing scheme. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A joint-check option 'in their sole discretion' with an express disclaimer of any contract, obligation or right in favour of the subcontractor. Clear and self-limiting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exhibit is headed 'construction costs to be reimbursed include' and then says 'The cost for all hand tools not customarily owned by the construction workers shall be borne by the Contractor', immediately followed by 'A flat rate of 5% shall be added to payroll costs to cover the cost of these hand tools' — the Contractor bears the cost and is simultaneously paid a 5% markup for it. judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits Applications to include amounts authorized by Construction Change Directives or interim determinations. Clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, carefully hedged statement of what a Certificate does and does not represent, with four express disclaimers. Detailed but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.9, which makes the same disclaimers, and 9.5.1; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits withholding 'to the extent reasonably necessary to protect the Owner' on an enumerated list ending with 'persistent failure to carry out the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents', and includes 'reasonable evidence that the Work cannot be completed for the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum'. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.1.1/5.2.1, where there is no stated Contract Sum or GMP against which to test whether the Work 'can be completed for the unpaid balance', and against 12.1.7.6. Real difficulty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When the above reasons for withholding certification are removed, certification will be made for amounts previously withheld.' Plain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Owner shall pay 'in the manner and within the time provided in the Contract Documents'. Entirely referential.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.3, whose payment-day fill-ins are blank or garbled, and First Addendum 12.2.2; the time it points to was never fixed for progress payments. Real gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prompt pay-through obligation to Subcontractors reflecting retained percentages, with a flow-down requirement. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.8 (subcontractor retainage of not less than 10%) and First Addendum 12.1.7.3 (5% on the Fee); the retainage figures differ but apply to different amounts. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: No Owner or Architect obligation to pay Subcontractors 'except as may otherwise be required by law'. Clear with a statutory saving.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Treats material suppliers in a manner 'similar' to Subcontractors. 'Similar' is loose but the reference is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.6.2-9.6.4 and Supplementary Conditions 9.6.2.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A non-acceptance rule for payment, partial use or occupancy. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.9.3 and 9.10.4; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.6.2 (pay-through duty) and Supplementary Conditions 9.6.2.1 (joint checks); the disclaimers sit consistently with the no-privity structure. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stop-work right if the Architect does not certify within seven days 'or if the Owner does not pay the Contractor within seven days after the date established in the Contract Documents', with the Contract Sum increased by shutdown, delay and start-up costs 'plus interest as provided for in the Contract Documents'. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.3 (payment dates blank or garbled), First Addendum 12.2.2 and Agreement 14.2 (interest rate line left blank); a powerful stop-work remedy hangs on two dates and a rate the Contract Documents never fixed. Real incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Substantial Completion is 'the stage ... when the Work ... is sufficiently complete in accordance with the Contract Documents so that the Owner can occupy or utilize the Work for its intended use'. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 4.3 (fixed date), 4.4 (bonus for early completion) and First Addendum 12.2.1 (recorded Notice of Completion); the definition drives a bonus, a deadline and final payment. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a 'comprehensive list of items to be completed or corrected', with omission not altering the obligation to complete. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.8.3-9.8.4 and 12.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An inspection procedure with a re-inspection loop if items are 'not sufficiently complete'. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.8.1 and 9.8.4; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Certificate 'shall establish the date of Substantial Completion' and fix responsibilities for security, maintenance, utilities, damage and insurance, and warranties commence then 'unless otherwise provided in the Certificate'. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 4.3/4.4, 9.8.5 and 12.2.2 (one-year correction period running from Substantial Completion); several consequences turn on a document whose content is discretionary. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: On acceptance and surety consent 'the Owner shall make payment of retainage applying to such Work', adjusted for incomplete or nonconforming Work. Clear mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.1.7.3, where retainage on the Fee is 'N/A', First Addendum 12.1.7.3 (5%) and Agreement 12.1.8 (10% for Subcontractors); what retainage is payable depends on which of the conflicting figures governs. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A joint inspection before partial occupancy to record the condition of the Work. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.9.3 and 11.4.1.5 (insurer consent to partial occupancy); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Partial occupancy is not acceptance of noncomplying Work 'unless otherwise agreed upon'. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.6.6 and 9.9.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A final inspection and certification procedure with the Architect certifying that the Work has been completed and 'the entire balance found to be due the Contractor ... is due and payable'. Detailed and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.2.3 (whose time periods supersede 9.4.1 and which routes the final accounting through the Owner's accountants), Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 (Owner acceptance of warranties) and First Addendum 12.2.1/12.2.2; four documents describe the final-payment gateway differently. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of five submittals closing with '(5) if required by the Owner, other data establishing payment or satisfaction of obligations ... to the extent and in such form as may be designated by the Owner'. A wholly Owner-defined residual item after a specific list is a general-versus-specific point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.4(b)/12.2.1/12.2.2 and Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1; the conditions on final payment accumulate across documents without a single controlling list. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits partial payment where final completion is 'materially delayed through no fault of the Contractor', with such payment not constituting a waiver of claims. 'Materially delayed' is the soft term.
