judgments.reasoning_cat1: Final payment waives all Owner Claims 'except those arising from' three enumerated categories, including 'failure of the Work to comply with the requirements of the Contract Documents'. The third exception is broad enough that the scope of the waiver is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.10 (consequential damages waiver), 12.2.5 (obligations not limited by the correction period) and 13.7.1; several overlapping waiver and limitation provisions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Acceptance of final payment waives all claims 'except those previously made in writing and identified by that payee as unsettled at the time of final Application for Payment'. The identification requirement is a strict, easily missed condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 12.2.4 (30-day arbitration demand or the accountants' figure becomes binding) and 4.3.2's 21-day rule; three separate forfeiture mechanisms bear on the same claims. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contractor shall be responsible for initiating, maintaining and supervising all safety precautions and programs.' Clear and absolute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1, which disclaims Owner responsibility for safety notwithstanding the Owner's expanded approval rights; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable precautions' and 'reasonable protection' against damage to three enumerated categories of persons and property. Conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.2.2-10.2.3 and 3.18.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A compliance-with-safety-law obligation. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.7.2 and 10.2.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable safeguards ... as required by existing conditions and performance of the Contract', with an illustrative list. Ordinary softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.2.1-10.2.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires 'utmost care' where explosives or 'other hazardous materials or equipment or unusual methods' are necessary; the text is truncated here and 'unusual methods' is undefined. Both the truncation and the standard are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.3.1-10.3.3 (hazardous materials) and 3.3.1; the provisions overlap without conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires designation of a responsible safety member, presumed to be the superintendent. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.9.1 and First Addendum Article 2 [Revised], which requires one designated supervisory employee for the project; the two designations may or may not be the same person. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not load or permit any part of the construction or site to be loaded so as to endanger its safety.' Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.2.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Triggered where 'reasonable precautions will be inadequate to prevent foreseeable bodily injury or death' from a material 'including but not limited to asbestos or polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)' — an illustrative list attached to a predictive standard. Both elements are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.3.2-10.3.3 and 10.4; the scheme is internally consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed procedure for verification, objection to proposed persons, resumption of Work on written agreement, and equitable adjustment of Time and Sum for shutdown, delay and start-up. Long but concrete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An Owner indemnity 'to the fullest extent permitted by law' conditioned on the material in fact presenting the described risk and 'provided that such damage, loss or expense is not due to the sole negligence of a party seeking indemnity'. judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes Owner responsibility for materials 'brought to the site by the Contractor unless such materials or substances were required by the Contract Documents'. Clear allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 10.3.1-10.3.3 and 3.5; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: In an emergency the Contractor 'shall act, at the Contractor's discretion, to prevent threatened damage, injury or loss', with compensation determined under 4.3 and Article 7. A discretion-plus-duty formulation, but clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 7.7.2 [Revision], which reimburses emergency costs 'only to the extent not ... capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition', and against Agreement 7.7.2; the Addendum materially narrows the compensation this clause preserves. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eight-item enumeration of claims to be insured against, with no limits stated in the clause itself. Precise as a list of coverages.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 16, which is entirely blank as to required limits of liability and bonds, and against 11.1.2; the enumeration is unaccompanied by any figure anywhere in the Contract Documents. Real gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Insurance must be 'written for not less than limits of liability specified in the Contract Documents or required by law, whichever coverage is greater', maintained without interruption to final payment. The comparison rule is clear if both inputs exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires certificates 'acceptable to the Owner' filed before commencement, with 30 days' notice of cancellation and continuation certificates 'if reasonably available'. 'Acceptable to the Owner' and 'reasonably available' are the soft terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Optionally, the Owner may require' this coverage, with reimbursement by increasing the Contract Sum, and minimum limits 'equal to the aggregate of the limits required for Contractor's Liability Insurance under Clauses 11.1.1.2 through 11.1.1.5'. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A waiver of rights among Owner, Contractor and Architect 'to the extent damages are covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance'. Conditional and self-limiting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated all-risk coverage list 'including, without limitation' a series of named perils. The 'without limitation' opener makes the list illustrative, which is deliberate rather than defective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.4.1 and Supplementary Conditions 11.4.1.1.1 (tools and construction equipment excluded); consistent as a narrowing. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: If the Owner does not intend to purchase the coverage it must so inform the Contractor in writing before commencement, failing which it bears 'all reasonable costs properly attributable thereto'. Clear conditions and consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 11.6, which states a parallel but reciprocal cost-shifting rule, and 11.4.1; two overlapping rules for the same failure. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This property insurance shall cover portions of the Work stored off the site, and also portions of the Work in transit.' Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 11.4.1.1.1 (tools and construction equipment on site excluded) and Agreement 7.5.6/12.1.7.2; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.9.1-9.9.3; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.10 (mutual consequential damages waiver, which already waives Owner losses of use) and 11.4.7; the waivers overlap and are stated with different conditions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires waiver in accordance with 11.4.7 where the Owner insures adjacent property separately, with endorsements. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.4.7 and 11.4.1; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Owner to file policy copies with the Contractor 'before an exposure to loss may occur' and to include cancellation and reduction notice provisions. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.1.3 (the mirror obligation on the Contractor) and Supplementary Conditions 11.6; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad mutual subrogation waiver extending to consultants and separate contractors, effective 'even though that person or entity would otherwise have a duty of indemnification ... and whether or not the person or entity had an insurable interest'. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.18.1 (Contractor's indemnity) and Supplementary Conditions 11.4.1.1.1, which requires the Contractor's own equipment policy to include a waiver 'in accordance with the requirements of Paragraph 11.4.7'; the waiver and the indemnity cut against each other. judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.4.7 and 9.6.7; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.2.2.1-12.2.2.2 and 12.2.5; the neighbouring provisions show what was intended, but the text as written contradicts them. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contract shall be governed by the law of the place where the Project is located.' Definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is heavily damaged, but the substance — mutual binding of successors and assigns, no assignment of the Contract as a whole without written consent, and continuing liability if assigned anyway — is conventional. The damage is the main difficulty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reduced to disconnected fragments in this text; the tests-and-inspections obligation and the associated approvals cannot be reconstructed from the words given. The defect is one of incompleteness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tests 'shall be made promptly to avoid unreasonable delay in the Work'. Ordinary softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.5.5 and 8.3.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.2.1, 5.4.1 (assignment of subcontracts) and Agreement 13.3; the machinery interlocks. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum exceeds costs of finishing the Work ... such excess shall be paid to the Contractor', with the amount 'certified by the Architect upon application'. The arithmetic is clear; its inputs are not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.2, which prescribes a different computation (Cost of the Work to termination plus a ratio-based Fee less previous payments) and caps it by the Guaranteed Maximum Price, and against 9.1.1/5.2.1 where no Contract Sum or GMP is stated. Two incompatible formulas for the same payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits suspension 'without cause ... for such period of time as the Owner may determine'. Unlimited Owner discretion is a one-sided term but plainly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.4, which requires the GMP and Contract Time to be increased on suspension, and 14.1.2 (termination after prolonged suspension); the compensation route depends on a GMP stated as 'N/A'. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Owner may, at any time, terminate the Contract for the Owner's convenience and without cause.' Short and unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.1, which caps the amount payable under A201 14.1.3 at the for-cause figure, and against 14.4.3, which promises overhead and profit on Work not executed; the consequence of exercising this right is described inconsistently. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated duties on receipt of a convenience-termination notice, including ceasing operations 'as directed by the Owner in the notice'. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.3 (assignment of subcontracts as a condition of payment) and 5.4.1; the direction to terminate subcontracts and the Owner's right to take assignment sit close together. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entitles the Contractor to 'payment for Work executed, and costs incurred by reason of such termination, along with reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed'. 'Costs incurred by reason of such termination' and 'reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed' are both open-ended measures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 13.1, which caps convenience-termination payment at the for-cause amount 'except that the Contractor's Fee shall be calculated as if the Work had been fully completed', and against 4.3.10, whose consequential damages waiver applies 'without limitation, to all consequential damages due to either party's termination in accordance with Article 14'. Three provisions give three different answers on the same payment.
